items.title: Bhotekoshi Floods: 677 transport workers unaccounted for
items.summary: Kathmandu, September 18 The Nepal Truck Transport Entrepreneurs Federation has reported that 677 workers are unaccounted for following the Bhote Koshi floods. The Federation disclosed this information during a meeting held on Thursday—coordinated by Rajiv Pokharel, Director General of the Department of Transport Management. items.title: 898 hydropower workers remain missing after Bhotekoshi floods
items.summary: Kathmandu, September 18 Twenty-two days after floods swept through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river corridors, 898 people working at 13 hydropower projects remain unaccounted for. According to data collected by the Nepal Engineers’ Association, 188 of those missing are engineers and technicians. items.title: Wagle seeks India’s support for post-flood reconstruction
items.summary: In his first foreign visit as finance minister, Wagle asks Sitharaman for help in rebuilding infrastructure destroyed by the Bhotekoshi floods and discusses trade, investment and connectivity.

items.title: Bhotekoshi floods disrupt schooling for 14,500 children in three districts
items.summary: More than 9,400 students have been directly affected, while schools being used as shelters are delaying the return to classes for thousands more.

items.title: Bridges gone, roads damaged, villages cut off from relief
items.summary: Helicopters and temporary crossings are helping deliver food and other essentials to cut-off communities in Rasuwa and Nuwakot, but officials say restoring roads and bridges must be an immediate priority.
